analysis.plain_explanation: You have been targeted by an online investment scam where fraudsters promise high returns through a fake trading app and then demand extra money under the guise of taxes when you try to withdraw your funds. This is a common form of financial fraud and online cheating. You can report this immediately to the national cyber crime reporting helpline and your bank to block further transfers and try to freeze the stolen funds. Recovering lost money from unauthorized scams is very difficult, and there is no guarantee of getting a refund. Be cautious of anyone claiming they can recover your money for a fee, as these are often secondary scams.

steps.title: Report financial fraud on the Cyber Crime Portal and helpline
steps.detail: Immediately report the scam on the cybercrime.gov.in portal or call the 24x7 toll-free helpline 1930. Provide all transaction details, bank account numbers where you transferred the money, and app screenshots to help authorities freeze the funds.
steps.where: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or call 1930

steps.title: Inform your bank immediately
steps.detail: Contact your bank's fraud helpline or branch at once to report the fraudulent transactions, give them the transaction references, and request them to flag or freeze the beneficiary accounts if possible.
steps.where: Your bank's official customer care or local branch

steps.title: (General) File a police complaint for online cheating
steps.detail: Submit a formal written complaint with your evidence package including bank statements, chat transcripts, and app screenshots to your local police station or cyber cell for investigation under Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
steps.where: Local police station or Cyber Crime Cell

steps.title: (General) Seek free legal aid or guidance
steps.detail: If you need professional assistance on what steps to follow next without high costs, contact the national legal aid helpline or your District Legal Services Authority.
steps.where: NALSA helpline 15100 or local District Legal Services Authority (DLSA)
